title: 🏛️ Exams 2001–2026 · telling the past: simple past or past progressive ⭐⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2026, general) Prasiddhi, a 12-year-old girl, has planted thousands of trees across India. She began when she was seven and a cyclone had destroyed thousands of trees. Which form completes the sentence? "As her passion ___, so did her ambitions."
questions.explanation: The story of her first trees is told in the past, and "so did her ambitions" is a past form too. Grow is irregular, so the simple past is grew. "grows" is a present form; "growed" adds -ed to an irregular verb; "will grow" is a future form.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025, general) A text on teenagers and technology compares today with the past. Which form completes the sentence? "Twenty years ago teens ___ much more time outside and enjoying sporting activities rather than swiping through social media."
questions.explanation: "Twenty years ago" is a finished time, so the simple past is needed. Spend is irregular: spent. "spend" is a present form; "spended" adds -ed to an irregular verb; "have spent" is a present perfect, which never goes with "ago".

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024, general) A mother tells how computer games ruined her teenage son Connor's life. Which form completes the sentence? "His obsession with living in a virtual world was ___ his education and consuming his life."
questions.explanation: After was, the verb takes -ing, as "consuming" does in the same sentence: the obsession was destroying his education during those years. "destroyed" cannot follow was here, because he is not the one destroyed; "destroy" leaves the base form after was; "been destroying" is not a form that follows was.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024, technical) Monique Strong grew up with a father in the construction industry in California, and her teachers advised her to join a technical college. Which form completes the sentence? "After graduating, she ___ a new job in building."
questions.explanation: The whole story is told in the past: she grew up, her teachers advised her, and then she graduated. Begin is irregular: began. "begins" and "begin" leave the verb in the present; "begun" is the past participle, which needs have before it.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2023, technical) Gilbert wants to be a welder. As a child he lived in poverty with his grandmother in Spain. Which form completes the sentence? "Then things ___ worse after he got ill."
questions.explanation: "after he got ill" puts the story in the past. Become is irregular: became. "become" is the base form (and the participle), not a simple past; "becomed" adds -ed to an irregular verb; "made" is the past of make, which would need an object ("things made him worse"), while the sentence says that things changed.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021, technical) A woman who is now a car mechanic remembers the jobs she had before 2014. Which form completes the sentence? "I worked in several car companies and with each job I did, I ___ very useful knowledge."
questions.explanation: She is looking back at jobs she did in the past: "worked" and "did" are past forms, so the simple past is needed, gained. "gains" is a present form; "gaining" cannot be the only verb of the clause; "will gain" is a future form.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2001) Emma Woodhouse was pretty and rich and lived with her father in a large house. Which form completes the sentence? "Emma's mother ___ when Emma was very young, so she felt lonely."
questions.explanation: A verb is needed, and the story is told in the past, as "when Emma was very young" shows: died, a regular verb with -ed. "dies" leaves the verb in the present; "dead" is an adjective and "death" is a noun, so neither can be the verb of the clause.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2010, technical) Diana had an interview with a local company. A boy from her old school also had an interview, and he got the job. Which form completes the sentence? "A boy from her old school also had an interview that ___ fourty-five [sic] minutes."
questions.explanation: The interviews are finished ("had", "got"), so the verb of the clause is in the simple past: lasted, a regular verb with -ed. "last" and "lasts" are present forms; "lasting" cannot follow "that" as the only verb.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2019, technical) Katie Gillard has always wanted to be a truck driver. People laughed at her when she passed her first driving test. Which form completes the sentence? "A lot of teasing went on where she ___, but Katie was happy doing her job."
questions.explanation: The story is told in the past, and her work was going on while the teasing happened: the past progressive, was + verb in -ing, with "she". "is working" and "will work" are a present and a future form; "were working" uses a plural auxiliary with a singular subject.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2016, general) In 1960, Sir Julian Huxley came back from a research trip to Africa, shocked by the hunting of rare animals. Which form completes the sentence? "The following year, Huxley, some fellow scientists and a few politicians ___ the World Wildlife Fund."
questions.explanation: To found an organization is to create it, and this regular verb makes its past with -ed: founded. "found" is the simple past of find (to discover), a different verb with a different meaning; "finding" has no auxiliary, so it cannot be the verb of the clause; "finded" adds -ed to an irregular verb.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2015, general) Daisy's father was restless and kept moving the family all over the country. More than once Daisy found her parents waiting for her after school, with the car packed. Which form completes the sentence? "With no warning, they ___ again."
questions.explanation: The story is told in the past, so a present or a future form does not fit. The car is already packed: they are in the middle of leaving, which is the past progressive, were + verb in -ing. "was moving" uses a singular auxiliary with "they"; "move" is a present form; "will be moving" is a future form.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2005) It was late and David was driving home from work, tired. Which pair completes the two gaps? "Another car came from the opposite direction and ___ into his car. David ___ out of his car and looked at the damages."
questions.explanation: The accident is told in the past, as "looked" shows. Run is irregular: ran; jump is regular: jumped. "run / jumped" leaves the first verb in the present, "ran / jump" the second one; "run / jump" leaves both in the present.
